results.name: nonrule_set_below_minus_above_extension
results.description: In sets of 2+ examples with no small common rule, yes rate for non-example targets 1-15 below the smallest example minus 1-15 above the largest; observed above the null means people extend number ranges downward more than the model's symmetric intervals predict (below = upward more).

results.name: decade_crossing_near_contrast
results.description: For non-example targets 1-5 from the nearest example, yes rate when the target is in the same tens decade (floor((n-1)/10)) as that example minus when it crosses a decade boundary; observed above the null means people treat decades as category boundaries the model ignores (below = decade boundaries matter less than the model predicts).

results.name: rule_set_near_nonmember_yes
results.description: In sets of 2+ examples sharing a small familiar rule, yes rate for non-member targets within 1-3 of an example; observed above the null means people's similarity-based leakage around examples exceeds the model's intervals plus noise (below = they reject near non-members more firmly than the model).

results.name: rule_member_yes_three_four_minus_two_examples
results.description: Yes rate for non-example members of the common small rule in sets of 3-4 examples minus in sets of exactly 2 examples; observed above the null means added examples strengthen rule generalisation more than the model's size principle predicts (below = examples accumulate less evidence for the rule than the model assumes).

results.name: rule_set_nonmember_inside_span_yes
results.description: In sets of 2+ examples sharing a small familiar rule, yes rate for targets inside the examples' span that are NOT rule members; observed above the null means people mix in magnitude-range generalisation alongside the rule more than the model does (below = they commit to the rule more strictly than the model).

results.name: near_outside_yes_vs_set_range_slope
results.description: Among non-rule sets of 2+ examples, least-squares slope of yes on the set's range (max-min, per 10 units) for non-example targets 1-10 outside the span; observed above the null means wide example spreads boost nearby generalisation more than the model's interval-size principle predicts (below = less).

results.name: rule_member_below_minus_above_span
results.description: In sets of 2+ examples sharing a small familiar rule, yes rate for non-example rule members below the smallest example minus those above the largest; observed above the null means people extend a rule toward smaller numbers more than the model's direction-symmetric runs predict (below = they extend upward more).

results.name: rule_member_far_minus_inside_span
results.description: In sets of 2+ examples sharing a small familiar rule (<=16 members), yes rate for non-example rule members more than 15 from every example minus yes rate for non-example rule members inside the examples' span; observed above the null means people generalise a rule to distant members more evenly than the span-restricted runs predict (below = they localise the rule even more than the model).
